transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 15:30 PST; duration 48m; attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Product), Elliot Park (Acme CTO), Sana Kapoor (ML Eng), Ravi Patel (Infra), Jules Romero (PM)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough, focus on quantization profiles: INT8 vs FP8; show quality/latency numbers, explain where dedicated vs hosted matters, and align on pilot scope.

00:00 - 00:18 Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, we appreciate you carving out time, today it is gonna be a hands-on Optimize walkthrough focusing on quant profiles int8 and fp8 and the quality versus latency tradeoff, marcus will go deep into numbers
00:19 - 01:02 Marcus: yeah hi all, Marcus Chen here, I'll share my screen in a sec, first quick qual, Elliot can you remind us your primary SLA target for production latency and the typical prompt length?
01:03 - 01:21 Elliot: yeah sure, we're shooting for sub-450ms token latency on average for our chat flow, prompts range 300 to 2k tokens but the typical 95th is about 900 tokens, some multimodal-ish long inputs too
01:22 - 01:45 Ava: great that's helpful; ace, and budget sensitivity? cost per 1M tokens would matter obviously, and whether you lean dedicated vs hosted?
01:46 - 02:20 Jules: we're fairly cost conscious; we'd prefer hosted if it meets latency but open to dedicated for consistent tail latencies; security is also a must — we need SSO, KMS, and audit logs
02:21 - 02:50 Marcus: perfect — we'll focus on the Optimize console profiles; note that 'FP8' profile in our tests gives the best latency but sometimes small quality regressions depending on model and instruction types; INT8 is more conservative — better quality, slightly higher latency
02:51 - 03:30 Marcus: (screen share) here's the Optimize UI, you can select a model family, then quantization profiles — we have prebuilt profiles for INT8, FP8, and hybrid. The console shows throughput, median latency, and quality delta vs baseline fp32 across your eval set
03:31 - 04:05 Sana: couple quick Qs — are these profiles auto-generated per model or generic? we run a custom Llama variant with some adapter layers
04:06 - 04:52 Marcus: good Q — we maintain catalog-level profiles, but Optimize can generate a bespoke profile during our onboarding: we run a calibration pass on a few hundred prom pts and then produce a quant profile tuned to your model weights; for adapter layers there can be corner cases where we keep some layers in higher precision
04:53 - 05:30 Ava: to add — for private customers we also do a brief validation job inside the VPC, so nothing leaves the network during profiling if you choose Private/Dedicated
05:31 - 06:10 Marcus: ok i'll flip to the benchmark numbers — note these are illustrative from a previous pilot; baseline fp32 is our "control" quality. INT8 profile shows 1.6x token throughput vs fp32, FP8 shows ~2.1x throughput, median latency improvements of 30-45% depending on sequence length
06:11 - 06:48 Marcus: quality delta: with FP8 on our internal eval set we saw a 0.8-1.5% drop in exact-match style metrics on instruction tasks; INT8 was within 0.2-0.6% of fp32 for most tasks. However on some arithmetic or hallucination-sensitive tasks FP8 occasionally had a bigger delta
06:49 - 07:25 Ravi: does that quality delta correlate with prompt length or with attention patterns? our workloads have a lot of long-context retrievals
07:26 - 08:08 Marcus: good point — we see FP8 sensitivity increase with long context and deep KV cache usage; KV cache correctness is stable but subtle rounding can affect generation in edge cases. For long retrievals we often recommend hybrid profiles — keep first/last n layers at higher precision
08:09 - 09:00 Marcus: also batching changes things — batching increases throughput but can hurt latency SLOs for tail; Optimize suggests per-route batching and dynamic policies. The Console shows per-route recommendations for batch size to hit SLOs
09:01 - 09:35 Jules: if we go dedicated, is it possible to pin a profile per route? e.g., inference endpoint A uses INT8, endpoint B uses FP8 for higher quality?
09:36 - 10:10 Marcus: yes you can pin quant profiles per route in the Console; we also support automated fallback: if a profile underperforms quality thresholds, the runtime can fall back to a higher-precision variant automatically
10:11 - 11:02 Marcus: quick demo: i'm running two parallel requests — FP8 vs INT8 — for a 800-token prompt, FP8 returns in ~420ms median and INT8 ~600ms on this node; quality-wise the FP8 output loses a few specificity tokens in one response
11:03 - 11:50 Sana: got it; how do we measure quality objectively? we use BLEU-like for some tasks and prefer human evals for chat coherency
11:51 - 12:30 Marcus: Optimize supports eval suites — you can upload prompt sets and reference outputs; we compute a set of measures (EM/ROUGE/BERTScore) and also surface qualitative diffs. We recommend a hybrid: automated metrics for broad regression detection and a smaller human eval sample focused on problem areas
12:31 - 13:10 Ava: and cost modeling — the console will show estimated token cost per million for each profile given throughput and compute; that helps product teams decide tradeoffs
13:11 - 14:00 Elliot: network-wise, if we choose Private, will Redwood run the profiling inside our VPC? earlier you said yes but need details on KMS and logs
14:01 - 14:40 Marcus: yes profiling can run inside your VPC for Private/Dedicated; KMS integration or HSM for keys is supported, and all audit logs are writable to your SIEM via syslog/S3; we'll share SOC2 artifacts
14:41 - 15:30 Ravi: fantastic — latency jitter is our main worry, do you have percentile metrics by device and can we get traces?
15:31 - 16:20 Marcus: Console provides P50/P90/P95 and per-token breakdowns, plus tracing hooks you can pipe into OpenTelemetry. For jitter we recommend reserved dedicated capacity with autoscale buffer and a small burst pool to avoid cold-start spikes
16:21 - 17:10 Marcus: returning to quant profiles: here's an example hybrid profile where layers 0-6 remain fp16 and layers 7-xx use int8, that gave us near-fp16 quality with a 1.8x throughput improvement in one case
17:11 - 18:00 Sana: any gotchas with finetuned or LoRA models? ours are LoRA adapters on top of Llama-2 style weights
18:01 - 18:45 Marcus: LoRA is generally fine; we sometimes keep the adapter layers in higher precision or apply per-tensor thresholds. Optimize's calibration step looks at per-tensor distribution and will suggest exceptions when needed
18:46 - 20:10 Marcus: demoing the quality vs latency graph — you can slide target quality tolerance and Optimize will propose profiles and expected latency/cost; also you can export results to CSV for deeper analysis
20:11 - 21:00 Ava: practical recommendation for Acme given your 900-token median and strict 95th tail: start with INT8 pilot on hosted to measure real workload, run FP8 as an experiment if cost pressure is high, and consider Dedicated if 95th tail exceeds SLOs
21:01 - 22:00 Elliot: sounds reasonable; can you run a benchmark with our prompts? we'll need to share a sample set and also allow you to run inside our VPC if needed
22:01 - 23:15 Marcus: absolutely — best path is you share 200-500 representative prompts (sanitized), we run a calibration and two runs: INT8 and FP8. We provide a per-prompt diff and a quality regression report plus latency histograms
23:16 - 24:30 Jules: for procurement timing — if pilot goes well what's an expected time to production?
24:31 - 25:20 Ava: pilot typically 2-4 weeks for profiling and validation, then production depending on whether you choose hosted or dedicated; dedicated provisioning can be 2-6 weeks depending on commit and capacity; we can accelerate with hot-start pool
25:21 - 27:00 Marcus: back to practicals — we'll also show you how to set alerts in Console: quality regression alerts tied to eval sets so you get notified if INT8 slips beyond your tolerance; we can also run automatic rollback to FP16/fp32 if needed
27:01 - 29:00 Sana: any special infra reqs for VPC profiler? e.g., egress rules, instance types, firewall rules
29:01 - 30:00 Marcus: minimal egress; we need a short-lived agent or a small container image we deploy in your VPC to access weights (or you can provide images on your side). For Dedicated we run on customer-owned subnets; we'll provide a config doc for Ravi
30:01 - 32:00 Marcus: (shows CSV export) here's sample perf spreadsheet — columns: prompt_id, prompt_len, fp32_q, int8_q, fp8_q, latency_fp32, latency_int8, latency_fp8, cost_est_fp32, cost_est_int8, cost_est_fp8. We'll populate this for your pilot and include per-prompt diffs
32:01 - 33:20 Ava: quick note on OSS models and licensing — if you're using community models we map license compatibility and will advise on distribution; if you need Redwood to host models privately we have Private deployment options
33:21 - 34:10 Elliot: any mention of competitor workflows we should be aware of — we evaluated ModelOpsInc and found their FP8 story a bit too aggressive and had regressions
34:11 - 35:00 Marcus: right; our approach is conservative with hybrid fallbacks and per-route policies so you can ship with confidence and roll back automatically if needed
35:01 - 37:10 Ava: ok let's outline next steps: we will send the perf spreadsheet, security docs, and a sample quickstart for profiling; Marcus will queue the benchmark and set up a dedicated pilot if you want; Acme to send prompts and infra details
37:11 - 38:00 Jules: timeline check — target pilot start next week if we can get prompts and approvals by Thursday
38:01 - 39:30 Marcus: we'll aim for a quick turnaround, calibration run is typically 24-72 hours after we have the sanitized prompts and model artifacts, full bench takes longer depending on scale
39:31 - 41:00 Sana: small detail — are there SDK hooks for embedding quality diffs into our CI so we can gate deploys?
41:01 - 42:00 Marcus: yes the Console has an API and webhooks; you can integrate a quality check into CI to block promotion if regression > threshold. We'll include docs and example scripts in the packet we send
42:01 - 44:00 Ravi: security ask — can we ensure keys never leave our KMS, and can you sign an NDA? also need SOC2 docs for procurement
44:01 - 45:10 Ava: yes we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; NDA is fine, we'll attach SOC2 and compliance pack in the follow-up email
45:11 - 46:30 Ava: quick recap: (1) Redwood sends perf spreadsheet, pricing, SOC2/security packet; (2) Acme sends 200-500 sanitized prompts + infra details; (3) Redwood runs INT8 and FP8 calibration and pilot; (4) schedule follow-up with results and decision on hosted vs dedicated.
46:31 - 47:30 Elliot: that works for us, thanks everyone.
47:31 - 48:00 Ava: great thanks all, we'll follow up with materials today/tomorrow and loop in solutions engineering for the pilot, bye

Notes: imperfect transcription present — product names occasionally mistranscribed (e.g., "Optimize" heard as "Opti-mize"), minor speaker label overlaps. References: "perf spreadsheet" (link provided in follow-up), security pack (SOC2) to be attached, sample quickstart for profiling will be shared.
